summary: The data shows high overall Time in Range (86.0%) but indicates a significant safety concern overnight, with Time Below Range reaching over 18% between midnight and 2 AM. The system is operating entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without any logged carbohydrates, which forces reactive microbolusing. This is compounded by unusually high safety limits for maximum Insulin on Board and maximum basal rates.
issues: Severe overnight hypoglycemia from 23:00 to 03:00, with glucose dropping as low as 41 mg/dL.
AAPS safety limits are set exceptionally wide (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h), allowing the pump to deliver large amounts of insulin unconstrained.
No carbohydrates are logged, meaning all meal insulin is delivered reactively via UAM.
GLP-1 use delays gastric emptying, causing late post-meal rises that UAM aggressively treats late in the evening, leading to overnight insulin stacking.
strengths: Excellent daytime Time in Range averaging over 80% to 90% most of the day.
Strong CGM data coverage (98.7%) with consistent pump communication.
System automation successfully brings down significant hyperglycemic spikes without manual intervention.
education: GLP-1 medications slow digestion, which means carbohydrates absorb over a longer, flatter curve. When carbohydrates are not announced, closed-loop systems struggle to predict this slow rise and often dose insulin too late.

Maximum IOB (Insulin on Board) and Maximum Basal rate act as safety ceilings. Setting them too high allows the system to stack dangerous amounts of insulin when it misinterprets a delayed meal rise as an extreme basal deficit.
A target of 90 mg/dL provides very little buffer against minor over-corrections, particularly while sleeping.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The Max IOB setting of 25 U is unusually high and poses a severe risk of hypoglycemia, particularly in combination with Dynamic ISF.
Adjustments should be made cautiously, especially if U200 dilute insulin is being used to bypass hardware delivery limitations.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent at 98.7% over 14 days. Loop telemetry is rich. User notes provide clinical context including GLP-1 1.25mg injections and a U200 dilute basal profile. However, there are absolutely zero logged carbohydrate entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero logged carbohydrates completely blocks analysis of Carb Ratios.

analysis_steps.findings: TIR is commendable at 86.0%, but Time Below Range (TBR) is elevated at 5.1%. Hypoglycemia risk is heavily clustered overnight: 23:00 (10.1% TBR), 00:00 (11.4%), 01:00 (18.5%), and 02:00 (10.1%). Extreme lows down to 41 mg/dL were recorded.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local TBR averages over 12% between 23:00 and 03:00.

analysis_steps.findings: A tight target of 90 mg/dL starts at 23:00, perfectly aligning with the onset of severe overnight TBR. Daytime TAR begins rising after midday when basal drops to 0.5 U/h, but lacking meal timing, we cannot confidently adjust daytime basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target drops to 90 at 23:00 leading into massive TBR. TAR spikes from 13:00-17:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of fasting tests and meal times makes it hard to distinguish true basal drift from unannounced evening meal stacking.

analysis_steps.findings: DIA is standard at 10h. ISF is a flat 56 mg/dL/U, but Dynamic ISF alters this aggressively. CR settings are dormant because no carbs are announced.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile array shows a single ISF segment at 00:00 (56 mg/dL/U). carb_treatment_entries is empty.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb data is missing, permanently blocking CR analysis.

analysis_steps.findings: The system relies entirely on UAM and SMB to handle all caloric intake. AAPS uses UAM logic to infer glucose deviations and deliver microboluses rapidly.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop telemetry frequently cites COB: 0 alongside UAMpredBG, Eventual BG, and UAM Boost driving SMB requests.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are exceptionally open. max_iob_units is 25 U and max_basal_u_per_hour is 12 U/h. Coupled with Dynamic ISF (70%), the system delivers aggressive insulin for unannounced evening meals, crashing the user overnight.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour = 12, max_iob_units = 25. Telemetry shows variable_sens down to 27.8 and rate at 4 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: The user executes a zero-announcement strategy. There are zero regular carbs and zero preboluses. The system reacts purely to CGM rises.
There are zero e-carb entries. Without e-carbs, the system cannot proactively model the delayed gastric emptying caused by GLP-1 therapy.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero extended carb treatments. User notes stating GLP-1 1.25mg.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or meal composition data.

analysis_steps.findings: The overnight hypoglycemia is the result of unannounced late-day meals (delayed by GLP-1) being aggressively treated by Dynamic ISF and UAM under massive safety limits (Max IOB 25U). Capping these limits and raising the overnight target are the required first steps.
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR peaks at 18.5% at 01:00. Limits are documented at 25 U and 12 U/h. Target is 90.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None blocking the primary safety recommendations.

recommendations.title: Reduce AAPS Safety Limits
recommendations.description: Max IOB of 25 U and Max Basal of 12 U/h are excessively high and allow the system to stack dangerous amounts of insulin for unannounced meals, driving overnight crashes. These must be lowered to safely constrain automated delivery.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL starting at 23:00 leaves zero buffer against hypoglycemia when UAM insulin is still active. Raising this provides a much-needed safety net while sleeping.

recommendations.title: Announce Carbohydrates
recommendations.description: Because GLP-1 delays digestion, reactive UAM struggles to dose safely. Logging carbohydrates (even without immediate bolusing) allows the algorithm's Carbs On Board (COB) logic to better predict the long, slow rise and prevent late-evening insulin stacking.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The 90 mg/dL target at 23:00 and 00:00 directly correlates with severe overnight hypoglycemia (up to 18.5% TBR at 1 AM). Raising the target provides a wider safety buffer against residual UAM insulin and basal drift.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight Time Below Range for 3 days to confirm hypoglycemia is eliminated before adjusting basal rates.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Change the 23:00 and 00:00 targets to 110 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user logs absolutely zero carbohydrates and relies purely on reactive AAPS Unannounced Meal logic. While this avoids meal logging, it causes late insulin stacking for GLP-1 delayed meals.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Begin logging estimated carbohydrates at the time of eating. Even if no immediate manual bolus is taken, giving the algorithm Carbs On Board (COB) data allows it to safely model the delayed absorption curve of GLP-1 therapy.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log all carbohydrate amounts and exact eating times for 7 days.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Reduce Max IOB to 7 U and Max Basal to 3 U/h to prevent dangerous automated insulin stacking.
Step 2: Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 glucose targets from 90 mg/dL to 110 mg/dL to build a safety buffer while sleeping.
Step 3: Monitor overnight glucose for 3 to 4 nights to ensure the severe hypoglycemia is eliminated.
Step 4: Begin logging estimated carbohydrates at meal times so the system can model slow GLP-1 absorption instead of reacting to it purely via UAM.
